newsitem.title: USA: Houston tightens restrictions on topless clubs.
newsitem.headline: Houston tightens restrictions on topless clubs.

text.p: Houston's city council Wednesday unanimously approved measures that could put most of the city's topless nightclubs out of business.

The ordinace doubles to 1,500 foot the buffer required between topless clubs and nearby neighbourhoods, a provision that would shut all but 26 of the 119 licensed clubs in Houston, city council members said.
So-called lap dances -- gyrating performances that bring big tips to the dancers -- also would be banned by a rule that would require customers to stay at least three feet away from the dancers.
In hearings last week, topless dancers packed council chambers to protest the regulations, and club owners have threatened to file suit to block the ordinance.
"I'm just wondering who will get to the courthouse first," Councilman John Kelley said.
"I think we've gotten completely out of the bailiwick of what we intended to do in the first place, and that was about tanning salons, the 24-hour (massage parlours) and so forth," Kelley said.

The tighter regulations were prompted by a proliferation of unlicensed tanning salons and massage parlours which police said were operating as fronts for prostitution. But the issue moved to the top of the city council's docket following complaints over plans by Rick's Cabaret to move into an affluent neighbourhood near Rice University.

Rick's, the only topless club trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange, posted revenues of $4.6 million last year. With its valet parking, marble floors and overstuffed chairs, Rick's is typical of upscale nightclubs that are as much a fixture in Houston as the oil industry and the Astrodome.
